name: Valley-floor temperate rain forest (Sitka spruce, western hemlock, bigleaf maple groves)

nature_serve: CES204.841 North Pacific Seasonal Sitka Spruce Forest
CES204.842 North Pacific Hypermaritime Western Red-cedar-Western Hemlock Forest
match.note: valley floors and river terraces of the Olympic west-side rivers (Hoh, Queets, Quinault, Bogachiel); the young alder flats and bars are pnw_braided_gravel_bar

narrative: Huge, widely spaced Sitka spruce and western hemlock over a floor that is mostly moss: moss on the ground, on every log, on the feet of the trunks, and on the maples so thickly that the limbs are fat green arms hung with streamers of clubmoss. Most young trees stand on logs, so living trees grow in rows and on stilts where an old log has rotted away. Elk keep it open: sword fern, oxalis and grass under the giants, few shrubs, sight lines between trunks. The light is soft and green, the air wet, summers foggy at dawn.

openness.v: park-like: widely spaced stems, openings up to several hectares

browse_pressure.unit: 0-1 (1 = shrubs held at a fifth of their unbrowsed cover)

browse_effect.v: after 36 years without elk: shrubs 5-6 fold, ferns +5-7 % cover, herbs -15-20 %, grasses under 1.5 %, salmonberry 0.2 -> 12 %

log_mats.v: thin (under 5 cm) on 59 % of a log, thick on 25 %

green_by_month.note: July has 66 mm of rain but dawn fog and drip; the moss dulls a little, never browns (the foothills' table goes to 0.1)

colour_lab.unit: CIELAB, the photo palette's three moss greens

living_vs_own_foliage.note: the foliage mass is from Oregon maples

alnus_rubra.note: ash-grey bark with white lichen patches

picea_sitchensis.note: moss on the lower limbs and buttresses; the crown stays dark blue-green

mortality.v: hemlock falls (windthrow); spruce dies standing, then falls

stilt_roots.v: conspicuous on trees born on logs: roots arch 0.5-2 m over the vanished log

quality.v: soft, diffuse, green-filtered; sun flecks rare; no hard shadows on overcast days (most days)

wet_season.v: 75-80 % of the rain November to April; July 66 mm

fog_drip_mm_yr.note: read only as a search snippet

fog.v: rolls in after sunset, lingers to late morning; summer

temp_c.unit: deg C, mean daily min and max

baseline_by_month.unit: 0-1 surface wetness without rain, January first

swatches.what: sky and mist through the canopy

green_hue_deg.unit: CIELAB hue angle of the green pixels, median

moss_green_share.unit: fraction of pixels with hue 95-125 deg and chroma over 14

group.what: cow herds with calves; bulls alone or in small groups; rut in September
